content.title: After the map
content.text: After the map we have a better idea of what sits inside AI. The part that matters for us is the centre: what the language models are built from. Trace the layers inward and we reach machine learning, and inside it neural networks. Everything else can go grey for now.

content.title: A very large network
content.text: A language model is a very large neural network with a particular wiring. Rows of small units, each row feeding the next. And a network can be stripped down to its smallest part: one unit, a neuron. Everything the network does is this unit, repeated.

content.title: A neuron
content.text: A neuron is a short series of calculations in a fixed order. Numbers come in. Several of them, each on its own wire: in a real network, the outputs of the row before. The neuron receives them and cannot change them.

numbers in, one per wire

content.title: Weights
content.text: Each number is multiplied by a weight: a number that decides how much that input counts. Near zero, the input is ignored. Large, it dominates. Negative, it is flipped. One weight per wire, and the weights belong to the neuron.

content.title: Add them up, add the bias
content.text: The results are added up into one total. Then one more number, the bias, is added to that total whatever the inputs were. It lets the neuron lean towards yes or no before it has looked at anything. One bias per neuron.

content.title: Squash: tanh
content.text: That total is then squashed. For decades the squash was tanh, a fixed curve that bends any number into the range from minus one to one. The bend is the point: without it, rows of neurons would collapse into one straight line and could not learn anything curved.

content.title: Squash: ReLU
content.text: Today most networks use ReLU instead. It does the same job more cheaply: negative numbers become zero, positive numbers pass through unchanged. And it keeps the learning signal alive through many layers, where tanh goes flat at both ends and the signal fades.

content.title: One output
content.text: Out of all that comes one number: the neuron’s output. That is all the next row will ever see of it. The weights, the sum, the bias and the squash stay inside.

content.title: A network repeats it
content.text: A network repeats this little calculation for every neuron, in rows, with the outputs of one row feeding the next. In a language model that is millions of neurons and billions of weights. Every one of those weights is a number that training will adjust. The next pills show how.
